title: Weyl's Theorem for Bounded Self-Adjoint Operators: the restriction lemma for spectral projections (printed as Lemma 4.3)
author: Hatem Baloudi, Mohamed Ali Dbeibia, Kamel Mahfoudhi
work: Weyl's Theorem for Bounded Self-Adjoint Operators
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Lemma 4.3 (source0.tex lines 595--608, source label lem:restriction), which the article itself introduces as the technical core of the paper: for a bounded self-adjoint operator on a quaternionic Hilbert space and a nonempty compact open part of its S-spectrum, the range and the kernel of the corresponding spectral projection are closed, mutually orthogonal and invariant, they decompose the space, their restrictions have the two parts of the spectrum as their spectra, and the two spectra are at positive distance when the complement is nonempty. It is delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 610--681 (72 lines, one adjacent proof environment, no gap and no deferral) and with the spectral theorem whose scalar measures the proof uses. The proof is a genuine argument in the quaternionic spectral theory developed by the article: it analyses the support of the scalar measure of a vector, shows that vectors supported in the compact open part generate exactly the range of the spectral projection, proves that this range and its orthogonal complement are invariant under the operator and that the operator splits accordingly, identifies the two spectra through the support of the measures, and obtains the positive distance between them from the compactness of the chosen part. The substantive steps are the support analysis, the splitting of the operator and the separation of the two spectra; none of them is an unpacking of definitions. H3: a complete original research-paper proof of the technical core of the paper, with its hypotheses and its invoked spectral theorem delivered.
